name: DPDP Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025
publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
description: India's personal data protection law. Applies to digital personal data processed in India, and to processing outside India when it relates to offering goods or services to people in India. The Rules are phased in: Data Protection Board from 13 Nov 2025, Consent Manager provisions from 13 Nov 2026, and the remaining obligations from 13 May 2027.

name: CERT-In Directions (April 2022)
publisher: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY
description: Directions on information security practices, procedures, prevention, response and reporting of cyber incidents. Apply to service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations.

name: RBI Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, Resilience and Assurance Directions (2026)
description: The RBI's cybersecurity and IT governance rules for regulated entities, issued on 31 July 2026 as one Direction per entity type: commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, urban co-operative banks, NBFCs, credit information companies and all-India financial institutions. In force immediately, with no transition period. Replaces the 2023 IT Governance Master Direction and the 2016 Cyber Security Framework. Fintechs that serve these entities are asked to meet the same controls through their contracts.

name: RBI Digital Payment Security Controls Directions (2026)
description: Security controls for digital payment products and services of banks and credit-card issuing NBFCs: governance, secure application development, customer authentication, fraud risk, reconciliation, customer protection, and specific controls for internet banking, mobile payment apps and card payments. They also cover non-financial digital actions such as balance enquiry, PIN set and change, and mobile banking registration. Non-bank payment system operators follow the separate PSO Directions.

name: RBI Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for Non-bank PSOs (2024)
description: For authorised non-bank payment system operators: payment aggregators, prepaid payment instrument (wallet) issuers, card networks, ATM and white-label ATM operators, Bharat Bill Pay operating units, TReDS, cross-border money transfer operators and others. Large PSOs had to comply by 1 April 2025, medium ones by 1 April 2026 and small ones by 1 April 2028. PSOs must also make their payment gateways, technology providers and vendors follow these controls.

name: RBI Payment Aggregators Directions (2025)
description: For banks and non-banks acting as payment aggregators (online, physical point-of-sale and cross-border): the baseline technology recommendations, card data rules, data localisation, annual cyber security audit, merchant due diligence, escrow and dispute handling. Payment gateways are recommended to follow the same technology baseline. Non-bank PAs also follow the RBI cyber resilience Directions for non-bank PSOs.

name: RBI Digital Lending Directions (2025)
description: For banks, co-operative banks and NBFCs that lend digitally, and the lending service providers (LSPs) and digital lending apps (DLAs) that work for them. Covers borrower data, consent, storage in India, app permissions, the Key Fact Statement, cooling-off, grievance redressal, LSP due diligence and reporting of apps to RBI. The regulated entity stays accountable for anything it outsources to an LSP.

name: RBI Outsourcing of IT Services Directions (2023)
description: How banks, larger NBFCs, credit information companies and all-India financial institutions manage IT outsourcing and cloud. Fintechs and SaaS vendors serving them are not regulated directly, but these requirements are passed to them in contracts: due diligence, audit rights for the bank and RBI, data in India, approval of sub-contractors, fast incident notification, business continuity and exit.

name: SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF)
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
description: Replaces earlier SEBI cyber circulars for stock brokers, depository participants, mutual funds, AMCs, KRAs, RTAs, portfolio managers, AIFs and market infrastructure institutions. Organised by the NIST CSF functions plus "Evolve". Requirements scale with the RE category; ISO 27001 certification, the Cyber Capability Index and red teaming apply to MIIs and Qualified REs.

name: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines (2026)
publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
description: IRDAI's cyber security rules for insurers and insurance intermediaries (brokers, corporate agents, web aggregators, TPAs), updated in April 2026 to replace the 2023 guidelines and to require DPDP compliance. Insurance agents, point-of-sale persons and surveyors are covered through the insurer's minimum security framework.

name: IFSCA Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Guidelines (2025)
description: For entities licensed or registered by IFSCA in GIFT City (banks, fund managers, brokers, fintechs, insurers and others), applied in proportion to their size. Branches of regulated entities, entities serving only their group and entities with fewer than 10 employees can rely on their parent's framework for three years, with an annual certificate from the designated officer.

name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
description: International standard for an Information Security Management System (ISMS). Certification requires the management system clauses (4 to 10) plus the applicable Annex A controls, justified in a Statement of Applicability.

name: SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria)
description: Attestation report on controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. Security (Common Criteria) is always in scope. Availability and Confidentiality are included by default; Processing Integrity and Privacy apply when you add them to your report scope (set this in your company profile).

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
description: A voluntary framework of cybersecurity outcomes grouped into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. Widely used by US customers and as a common language for security programmes. SEBI's CSCRF is built on the same functions.

name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
description: Security standard for any organisation that stores, processes or transmits payment card data, or can affect its security. Required by card brands and acquiring banks; RBI's payment aggregator and tokenisation rules also lean on it. Requirements dated 31 March 2025 are now mandatory.

name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI management system)
description: Certifiable standard for managing AI responsibly, for organisations that build, provide or use AI systems. Shares its management system structure with ISO 27001, so most governance controls carry over; the AI-specific controls cover impact assessment, data, lifecycle, transparency and suppliers.

name: EU GDPR (Regulation 2016/679)
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU
description: The EU's data protection law. Applies to organisations established in the EU, and to organisations outside the EU (including Indian companies) that offer goods or services to people in the EU or monitor their behaviour. Fines reach EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover.

name: HIPAA Security and Breach Notification Rules
publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
description: US rules for protecting electronic protected health information (ePHI). Apply to covered entities (health plans, providers, clearinghouses) and to business associates that handle ePHI for them, which includes Indian health-tech, BPO and SaaS companies serving US healthcare customers.
